improv_extras.concept: place particles on an aperiodic Penrose / quasicrystal tiling so the lattice never repeats yet stays ordered

v1.feedback: The Penrose P3 tiling is algorithmically correct and the bone/sage palette is well-chosen, but this reads as a fresh start — there is no visible DNA from parent x82's speculative topography, violating chain-mode's morph requirement. A refined version should seed the tiling from the parent's terrain-like elevation field, letting the quasicrystal emerge as a geological stratum within that topography rather than replacing it. The top-down fixed camera makes the piece feel like a screensaver tile demo; angling down at ~55° with slight depth-of-field would give the 'impossible floor' more spatial presence and let the breathing wave read as tectonic rather than decorative.

v2.feedback: Penrose deflation is correctly implemented and the bone/sage palette is well-restrained, but the form reads as a decorated floor plane viewed from a steep top-down camera — flatten the camera angle (lower Y, increase Z) to give the tectonic breathing wave actual silhouette against the horizon so the aperiodic structure reads as geology rather than tilework. The ghost city at opacity 0.16 is nearly invisible and contributes nothing; either raise it to ~0.28 with a slow vertical drift so it reads as archaeological echo, or remove it to avoid dead GPU draw calls. Consider giving the Penrose tiles slight per-instance Y-extrusion based on triangle type (golden vs gnomon) so the quasicrystal has volumetric relief the eye can parse in 2 seconds.
